summary: Release-readiness re-verification for director demo. Backend RBAC + multi-site isolation gates confirmed. Public /pulse-pricing page renders all 4 modules, flagship badge, currency+billing toggles, service-provider cards, FAQ, and ROI CTA (opens login modal). One UI bug found: ROI calculator sliders do NOT recompute the 'Estimated annual saving' text — the value stays at £6,912/yr regardless of slider changes (though the individual slider labels DO update).

ui_bugs.issue: Adjusting any of the three sliders (Machines in estate / Avg engineer callout / Callouts per month) does not update the [data-testid="roi-annual-saving"] value nor the sub-line 'X every month in avoided callouts'. Slider labels (e.g. '80' -> '85') do update, so the input state is bound but the derived saving calculation is NOT recomputed. Value stays frozen at £6,912/yr. Additionally the headline saving number in the dark card renders blurred/animated indefinitely (likely a CountUp animation stuck on initial mount).

issues: The large 'Estimated saving' number renders visually blurred (motion/CountUp animation appears not to settle) — the aria/textContent reads a static value while the visual shows a smeared number. Poor legibility for demo.

action_items: Fix ROI calculator: ensure Estimated annual saving recomputes on slider change (likely the useMemo/useEffect dependency array or the CountUp component is keyed to initial values only). Also verify the CountUp animation settles instead of rendering a blurred loop.
critical_code_review_comments: RBAC gate for clear_demo_data returns HTTP 403 correctly for logistics role with message 'This action requires one of: admin, manager, marketing_admin, operator, owner' — verified via automated test. Owner is allowed (not 401/403).

Multi-site filter enforces 403 site_access_denied for /api/equipment, /api/issues, /api/gym-health-score when a Site-A-restricted manager passes site_id=iso-demo-site-b — all three endpoints verified.
GET /api/payments/pricing/live is publicly reachable and returns pricing payload; front-end binds correctly (GBP £69/49/79, EUR €79/59/89, USD $99/69/119; annual = monthly*10).
ROI calculator computes 12 * £120 * 0.4 * 12 = £6912 as a constant — the value is not reactive to slider state; needs investigation in PulsePricingExtras.js.

success_rate.frontend: ~90% — all sections render & most interactions work; ROI slider→saving reactivity broken

test_credentials: owner@isodemo.com / IsoDemo123!, manager@isodemo.com / IsoDemo123!, logi1@isodemo.com / LogiPass123! (as provided in review request)
seed_data_creation: None. Owner clear_demo_data call was made with params.dry_run=true; response was non-403 (gate confirmed to allow owner).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend RBAC + site isolation are solid; do not re-test unless routes change. For frontend, focus on retesting the ROI calculator after fix — the sliders update React state for the value displayed next to their label, but the derived useMemo for 'saving' appears stale. Cookie banner is dismissible via button:has-text('Accept'). All other /pulse-pricing sections (modules x4, flagship badge, currency toggles GBP/EUR/USD, billing monthly/annual, service provider cards sp-card-*, FAQ items faq-item-0..5 with toggle expand) work as spec'd.
rca_of_the_issue: ROI annual saving frozen: the label numbers beside each slider update on drag/keyboard (so the range input is a controlled component with working onChange), but [data-testid=roi-annual-saving] never changes. Likely causes: (a) the annual saving is memoized against a stale dependency (e.g. hardcoded constants instead of the state variables), or (b) it's rendered inside a CountUp component whose 'end' prop is captured at mount and not re-keyed on value change. Fix location: /app/frontend/src/components/pulse/PulsePricingExtras.js — check the useMemo/useEffect and the CountUp end prop for the saving figure. Reproduction: open /pulse-pricing → scroll to 'See what Pulse pays back' → drag any slider; label updates but the black 'Estimated saving' card stays at £6,912/yr and £576/month.
